## Zoning Analysis: 3400 N Central Park Ave (PIN 13233160400000)

This parcel was resolved **authoritatively** from Cook County's address records, so all zoning and regulatory facts below apply directly to this PIN.

---

### 1. Zoning District

This parcel is zoned **RS-3 (Residential Single-Unit – Detached House)**. The RS-3 district is one of three RS tiers differentiated primarily by minimum lot area and floor area ratio [5]. You can verify this on the official Chicago Zoning Map: [https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning)

---

### 2. Could You Build a Two-Flat Here?

**Possibly, under a specific exemption — but it is not as-of-right in the typical sense.** RS-3 is a single-unit detached-house district; by default it accommodates one dwelling unit per lot. However, [1] provides a critical exception: in RS-3, the minimum lot area per dwelling unit **may be reduced to 1,500 sq ft** (enabling a two-unit building) when **60% or more of the zoning lots fronting on the same side of the street between the two nearest intersecting streets** have been lawfully improved with buildings containing more than one dwelling unit, **or** when the property falls within the "Predominance of the Block" boundaries as defined by §17-7-0591. This exemption only allows establishment of a **two-unit building** — not more.

The lot has 3,616 sq ft [assessor data], which would satisfy the 1,500 sq ft × 2 units = 3,000 sq ft threshold if the block-context exemption applies. **You would need to document the existing block conditions** to invoke this exemption. The existing building is already recorded as a 5-unit structure [assessor data], which itself may be a pre-existing nonconforming use — a separate legal question.

---

### 3. Key Bulk and Density Standards (RS-3)

The context does not include the full RS-3 bulk table (FAR, maximum height, front/rear/side setbacks are not explicitly provided in the retrieved code sections). Here is what can be confirmed from the context, and what cannot:

- **Minimum lot area per unit:** 2,500 sq ft as-of-right in RS-3 (the baseline for a single unit on a standard lot); reducible to **1,500 sq ft per unit** for a two-flat under the block-context exemption noted in [1].
- **Density limit on exemption:** The [1] exemption authorizes **only a two-unit building** even if lot math would allow more.
- **FAR, maximum height, and setbacks:** These are standard RS-3 bulk standards defined in §17-2-0400 and the RS-3 bulk table, which were **not returned in the retrieved code sections** — I cannot confirm specific numeric values here. Verify directly at the Chicago Zoning Portal or contact the Department of Planning & Development (DPD).
- **Off-street parking location:** In RS districts, off-street parking is **prohibited in side setbacks and within 20 feet of the front property line**, except that parking may be in a required side setback when accessed by a permitted driveway from the front [3]. Required residential parking must be on the same zoning lot as the dwelling units served [3].

---

### 4. Overlays and Special Designations

This parcel carries **four regulatory overlays**:

- **Special District** — The parcel is within a Special District overlay. The specific nature and requirements of this district were not detailed in the retrieved data; verify with DPD.
- **Transit-Oriented Development (CTA)** — The parcel is in a CTA TOD overlay area, consistent with its proximity (~0.25 miles) to the **Addison Blue Line station**. Under the Connected Communities Ordinance, TOD designation enables density and parking bonuses near transit. See item 5 below for parking implications.
- **ADU Eligible Area** — This parcel is in a designated ADU-Allowed RS Area, making it eligible for Additional Dwelling Units (conversion units and/or coach houses) subject to the conditions in [2] and [4]. See item 6.
- **Affordable Requirements Ordinance (ARO) Zone** — Any qualifying residential development trigger may require affordable unit set-asides or in-lieu fees. The Avondale community area has **6 ARO housing projects totaling 76 units**, including Hairpin Lofts (25 units), Milwaukee Ave. Apts. (32 units, supportive housing), and The Field's Lofts (12 units).

**Not applicable to this parcel:**
- No Planned Development
- Not a landmark or historic district building
- Not on the National Register of Historic Places
- Not in a Lakefront Protection Zone
- Not in a PMD (Planned Manufacturing District)
- Not in a Special Service Area
- **Flood zone: FEMA Zone X** — area of minimal flood hazard; not a Special Flood Hazard Area, so flood insurance is not federally required.

**Nearby brownfields:** Two EPA-listed brownfield sites are in the vicinity — **BNSF Little Village Paseo Segment 1** (EPA ID 110071982538) and **BNSF Little Village Paseo Segment 2** (EPA ID 110071982539). Environmental due diligence (Phase I/II ESA) is advisable before any significant ground disturbance.

---

### 5. Parking Requirement and Transit-Related Reduction

In RS districts, required off-street parking for residential uses must be on the same lot as the dwelling units served [3]. The TOD overlay (CTA) makes this parcel **eligible for parking reductions or waivers** under the Connected Communities Ordinance — the specific reduction formula depends on the proposed use and unit count and should be confirmed with DPD or reviewed under §17-10-0102 (TOD parking standards, not retrieved here). The assessor notes a **3-car garage** on the existing structure, which may already satisfy or exceed baseline requirements.

---

### 6. Coach House / ADU: Could You Add One?

**Yes, subject to conditions.** Because this parcel is in a designated **ADU Eligible Area** [2], a coach house (or conversion ADU) may be permitted in this RS-3 district — which would otherwise prohibit them under [4] ("a building permit for a new coach house unit may not be issued for any RS-designated zoning lot unless it complies with Section 17-7-0570"). The ADU area designation unlocks that pathway.

**Key limits and conditions under [4] and [2]:**

- **Maximum height:** Coach houses may not exceed **22 feet** in building height; rooftop features also capped at 22 feet overall above grade [4].
- **Side setback clearance:** At least **3 feet of open, unobstructed space** must be provided between the coach house and at least one side property line for the entire length of the building wall (except where a side line abuts an alley or street) [4].
- **Rear placement:** Coach houses in B/C districts must be in the rear 30 feet of lot depth [4] — in RS districts, the ADU section governs placement; verify with DPD.
- **Accessory parking:** Required parking for the principal building may be reduced/waived by administrative adjustment [4]; the coach house itself does not need to provide its own parking [4].
- **ADU program enforcement:** Compliance is enforced by the Department of Housing at the time of ADU pre-certification, per §2-44-106(g) [2].
- **Area-specific limitations:** Each ADU-Allowed RS Area may impose additional limitations (e.g., limits on number of new units, conversion-only vs. new construction) [2] — you must confirm what specific limits apply to this Avondale ADU area with the Department of Housing.

**How to verify:** Contact the Chicago Department of Housing ADU program or consult the ADU pre-certification process under §2-44-106(g). DPD's online zoning confirmation letter service can also provide a binding written determination.
